# Kome.Crypto known-answer vectors. Read by tests/test_crypto.adb.
# One vector per line, hex fields separated by single spaces, "-" for the
# empty byte string, "#" starts a comment line. Every value comes from a
# published test suite or from an implementation independent of monocypher:
#   blake2b256      Python hashlib.blake2b(digest_size=32) (RFC 7693 BLAKE2b).
#                   Lengths 127/128/129, 255/256/257 straddle the 128-byte block.
#   eddsa           monocypher 4's crypto_eddsa_* is RFC 8032 Ed25519 with
#                   BLAKE2b-512 in place of SHA-512 (monocypher.c
#                   crypto_eddsa_sign; SHA-512 Ed25519 lives in the optional
#                   monocypher-ed25519.c, which is not vendored). Seeds and
#                   messages are RFC 8032 section 7.1 TESTs 1-3; the public
#                   keys and signatures come from a pure-Python RFC 8032
#                   reference with the hash swapped, which reproduces the
#                   published SHA-512 TEST 1 answer (d75a9801..., e5564300...)
#                   when given SHA-512.
#                   The three vectors were also cross-checked by an
#                   independent reviewer's own pure-Python RFC 8032
#                   implementation with BLAKE2b-512 (all three match; with
#                   SHA-512 it reproduces the RFC's TEST 1).
#   eddsa_pk        Published Ed25519-BLAKE2b key pairs: nano-docs,
#                   docs/integration-guides/key-management.md (Nano's
#                   "ED25519 curve using Blake2b-512 as the hash function",
#                   the same scheme as monocypher's crypto_eddsa). The five
#                   "Derived Private Key" -> "Derived Public key" pairs of
#                   its two BIP39 examples, verbatim. Monocypher's own EdDSA
#                   vectors are generated at build time (ed25519-donna with
#                   ED25519_CUSTOMHASH = BLAKE2b) and not committed, so these
#                   are the published answers available for this variant.
#   ed25519_sha512  RFC 8032 7.1 TEST 1 verbatim. Kome.Crypto.Verify must
#                   REJECT it: it documents which EdDSA variant is bound.
#   x25519          RFC 7748 section 5.2 (cross-checked with pyca/cryptography).
#   x25519dh        RFC 7748 section 6.1 Alice/Bob exchange.
#   x25519_low      Low-order u-coordinates: 0, 1, the order-8 points
#                   e0eb7a7c... and 5f9c95bc... (libsodium's low-order
#                   blocklist; RFC 7748 §6.1 says to check for all zeros), p - 1, and the non-canonical encodings p and
#                   p + 1. Any scalar gives an all-zero shared secret
#                   (pyca/cryptography refuses every one with "Error
#                   computing shared key"), so X25519 must report
#                   Contributory = False.
#   aead            XChaCha20-Poly1305, IETF construction (monocypher 4
#                   crypto_aead_lock): the first line is
#                   draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha-03 appendix A.3.1; the rest are
#                   computed with HChaCha20 (checked against the draft's 2.2.1)
#                   plus pyca/cryptography ChaCha20Poly1305.
#
# Formats:
#   blake2b256     <msg> <digest32>
#   eddsa          <seed32> <public32> <msg> <sig64>
#   eddsa_pk       <seed32> <public32>
#   ed25519_sha512 <public32> <msg> <sig64>
#   x25519         <scalar32> <u32> <out32>
#   x25519dh       <alice_sk> <alice_pk> <bob_sk> <bob_pk> <shared>
#   x25519_low     <u32>
#   aead           <key32> <nonce24> <ad> <plain> <cipher> <mac16>
